Mednet gives me direct access to content experts beyond my own academic center. They share their approaches to complex dermatology questions and point to valuable clinical and basic science research. I use Mednet discussions to supplement my literature review and stay current with the latest advances in my field.

Mednet provides a wealth of information through experts in different fields of Neurology. This is super helpful to search for more detail on topics that we have seen on rounds, but more importantly, to know that the information is coming from experts in their field. Often, it's hard to find accurate answers to specific questions in textbooks, and that gap is being filled by Mednet.

It's great to read the varying perspectives from more than one colleague on the same topic and see where they diverge or converge in their opinions. Many of the topics are directly relevant to issues I face daily, so it has facilitated some quick literature review and helped me provide the best care possible for my patients.

I use this platform to get feedback on challenging clinical situations, gray areas where the data is not clear, or clinical situations where data is lacking. It's also nice to get expert opinions and interpretation of data. Bottom line, I come here to get answers to improve my practice and to learn!

Journal Clubs are a great way to keep up to date with the latest research and start a discussion about how to apply in clinical practice.

In partnership with ASCO and major medical publications (NEJM, Lancet, JCO, etc), Mednet is running online journal clubs where doctors get free, easy access to pivotal publications, and have the opportunity to engage with experts and study authors on the research and practice implications.
Periodically, Mednet will initiate discussion and solicit questions on a singular topic to provide a holistic expert view on a subject through Q&A.
In collaboration with select NCI cancer centers, we designed a process to capture knowledge and discussion from top cancer centers and share with the Oncology community.
Mednet is where physicians share the knowledge guidelines leave out, so every doctor can practice with the whole field behind them.

We connected with physicians who had extensive experience in the type of cancer our dad had been diagnosed with. Each physician was able to provide knowledge that's not always available in guidelines. This was knowledge based on their first-hand experiences and depth of research in treating like-patients. This was knowledge that could inform better decision-making throughout the treatment process.
